Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Marketplace launch readiness (CS + Support) - playbooks, escalation, ticket categories
Recorded: 2025-02-12 17:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees (Redwood): Jasmine Liu, Dev Patel, Rafael Mendes, Elliot Price, Talia Benson, Markus Klein, Allison Grant
Attendees (Eng/Other): Chloe Martin, Ethan Park, Leila Farouk

Summary (auto-generated):
Team aligned on the top expected support tickets for AWS/GCP Marketplace launch and reviewed proposed ticket categorization, escalation routing, and playbooks. SRE will own alerts for entitlement lag and webhook failures; Support will own intake templates/macros and initial triage; Eng will provide required identifiers and backfill scripts where needed. Docs will publish customer-facing FAQ/troubleshooting pages timed to listing go-live.

Topics:
- Expected ticket categories for marketplace buyers
- Intake checklist (what info Support must collect)
- Escalation routing and severity definitions
- SRE monitoring: entitlement lag, webhook failures, provisioning error rates
- Customer-facing templates and docs links
- Edge cases: wrong org linking, region mismatch, delayed entitlements, billing confusion

Action items (auto-generated):
- Dev to publish macros and tags
- Rafael to confirm on-call routing
- Elliot to finalize URLs
- Ethan to share AWS/GCP identifiers required for triage
- Leila to run staging E2E flows and document timing

Transcript:

[00:00] Jasmine Liu: Alright, thanks everyone. This is the CS and Support readiness sync for the cloud marketplace launch. Goal today is to make sure we don’t, uh, get surprised on day one with tickets we can’t route.

[00:14] Jasmine Liu: Dev, can you start with what you think the top ticket types are gonna be?

[00:18] Dev Patel: Yeah. So based on the previous “buy via marketplace” pilots and the staging tickets, we basically have five buckets.

[00:26] Dev Patel: One is entitlement activation delays. Like they purchase in AWS Marketplace, they come to Redwood Console, it still says “no entitlement found” or “pending”.

[00:37] Dev Patel: Two is wrong org linking. They link the AWS account to the wrong Redwood org, or they have multiple orgs and pick the wrong one.

[00:44] Dev Patel: Three is region mismatch. Mostly GCP, but AWS too, where they purchased in one region and then they’re trying to provision in another. And the Console copy is… better now, but it still confuses people.

[00:56] Dev Patel: Four is billing and invoice confusion. Like “why am I seeing charges in the marketplace but also something in Redwood,” or they’re asking about refunds and credits.

[01:05] Dev Patel: Five is security packet requests. “Send SOC2, pen test letter, encryption diagram,” all that. Those come in through Support sometimes, even though they’re kind of Sales-ish.

[01:16] Jasmine Liu: Yep, that matches what I’m seeing.

[01:19] Markus Klein: And also “what SKU do I buy.” Not exactly a support ticket but it will land on someone.

[01:24] Dev Patel: Yeah, true. That’s like pre-sales, but it shows up post-purchase too when they bought Hosted and then they expected Dedicated or VPC.

[01:32] Talia Benson: Can I just add—partners flagged that too. Like AWS reviewers ask, “is Dedicated separate SKU, is Private separate,” and customers will ask the same thing.

[01:42] Jasmine Liu: Okay. Let’s keep today focused on post-purchase activation and support motions, but we can add a macro for “SKU selection / route to Sales.”

[01:53] Elliot Price: For docs we’ll have a page that’s like, “AWS Marketplace onboarding” and “GCP Marketplace onboarding” plus an FAQ that points people to Sales for plan selection.

[02:02] Jasmine Liu: Great. So, Dev, on ticket categorization—what do you want in Zendesk?

[02:07] Dev Patel: I’d like a single top-level product area tag “Marketplace,” then sub-tags. Something like:

[02:12] Dev Patel: marketplace_entitlement_delay
marketplace_org_linking
marketplace_region_mismatch
marketplace_billing_invoicing
marketplace_security_docs
marketplace_sku_selection

[02:24] Dev Patel: And then provider tag: aws_marketplace or gcp_marketplace.

[02:29] Allison Grant: If you tag provider we can match to the dashboards. Like entitlement lag by provider.

[02:36] Jasmine Liu: Ethan, can you sanity check the entitlement delay path? What do we need from the customer to debug quickly?

[02:43] Ethan Park: Yeah. For AWS we need their AWS account ID ideally, but also the marketplace customer identifier. I’m blanking on the exact field name, we call it “customer id” in the payload. Sometimes the webhook has it.

[02:56] Ethan Park: We also need timestamp of purchase, and the product code / SKU ID. Because we map SKU IDs to internal entitlements. If they paste a screenshot of their AWS subscription page, that helps.

[03:09] Dev Patel: Can we put that in the macro? Like a checklist.

[03:12] Ethan Park: Yes. And for GCP, it’s… different. It’s like billing account / procurement account, and then the entitlement comes through their Pub/Sub message. Sometimes the region is the issue, not actually entitlement.

[03:27] Chloe Martin: From Console side, we show “pending activation” for up to, I think, 15 minutes and then we say contact support. But that 15 number might not be right.

[03:36] Rafael Mendes: In reality, the end-to-end pipeline p95 is like 3 to 7 minutes when it’s healthy. 15 minutes is safe, but it also means we’re telling them to wait too long if it’s broken.

[03:47] Jasmine Liu: So for Support, what’s our guidance? If they open a ticket at minute 5, do we tell them “wait,” or do we start triage?

[03:54] Dev Patel: We can do both. Macro can say: “Activation typically completes within 10–15 minutes. If it’s been longer than 15, please send X, Y, Z.”

[04:04] Rafael Mendes: I’d like us to start triage immediately if we see multiple tickets. Because that’s a signal something is down.

[04:12] Allison Grant: Yeah, that’s what the alert is for. If entitlement_lag_p95 crosses threshold, SRE gets paged regardless of tickets.

[04:20] Jasmine Liu: Rafael, can you outline the alerts we’ll have on launch day?

[04:24] Rafael Mendes: Sure. We have three primary signals in the marketplace provisioning pipeline.

[04:29] Rafael Mendes: One: webhook ingestion failures. That’s like validation errors, signature mismatch, payload parsing, whatever.

[04:36] Rafael Mendes: Two: entitlement lag timer. That’s from “marketplace event received” to “entitlement applied to org.” We track p50, p95.

[04:44] Rafael Mendes: Three: provisioning error rate in the Console flow. Like org linking fails, region mismatch errors, and unknown errors.

[04:52] Rafael Mendes: If webhook failures spike, it’s a Sev-1 because nothing will activate. If entitlement lag is high but still moving, could be Sev-2 depending on volume.

[05:04] Jasmine Liu: What’s “high” for lag?

[05:06] Rafael Mendes: We’re proposing p95 over 20 minutes for 10 minutes triggers page. And p95 over 10 minutes triggers Slack alert.

[05:15] Dev Patel: That seems reasonable. 20 minutes is definitely customer-visible.

[05:19] Leila Farouk: Just noting—on staging when the retry got stuck, it was like… it never completed. So p95 looks weird because it’s infinite.

[05:27] Rafael Mendes: Right, and that’s why we also alert on “stuck events count,” basically number of events older than 30 minutes.

[05:35] Jasmine Liu: Okay. Can you also confirm the escalation routing? Like Support gets a ticket, what do they do.

[05:41] Dev Patel: First line: Support checks if it’s within 15 minutes of purchase, asks for identifiers. If it’s an entitlement delay, we check internal status page / dashboards.

[05:50] Dev Patel: If dashboards show an incident, we respond with a known issue template. If not, we open an internal bug / page the on-call based on severity.

[05:59] Dev Patel: For wrong org linking, we need a remediation workflow. Right now it’s a manual fix by Console backend, I think.

[06:06] Chloe Martin: Yeah, it’s not fully self-serve yet. We can unlink and relink, but we need to verify identity.

[06:13] Markus Klein: That one is sensitive. We should be careful we’re not letting someone move an entitlement to a different org without proof.

[06:19] Jasmine Liu: Agreed. Chloe, what do you need from the customer to validate that?

[06:23] Chloe Martin: We need them logged into the Redwood org admin. Then we ask for a screenshot of the Marketplace linking page showing the AWS account ID, plus the org ID from the Console settings.

[06:34] Chloe Martin: Also we can ask them to paste the “linking token” if it exists. Sometimes it’s not shown. Sorry, I’m mixing builds.

[06:41] Dev Patel: That’s okay. We’ll keep macro flexible. The key is: prove you control the marketplace account and you’re admin of the target Redwood org.

[06:50] Jasmine Liu: Let’s talk about ticket severity and expected response times. I know we have Premium SLA add-ons in the new SKUs. How does Support handle that?

[06:59] Dev Patel: For now, we’ll just flag accounts that have premium support in our CRM and in Zendesk. If they’re premium, we treat entitlement activation issues as higher priority.

[07:09] Markus Klein: We need to be careful. Marketplace doesn’t always pass “premium support” as a separate entitlement day one.

[07:16] Ethan Park: It will, eventually, but yeah, it’s an add-on SKU mapping. We have the internal entitlement model, but the UI might not show it clearly at launch.

[07:26] Jasmine Liu: So operationally we can still do it by account list for the first couple weeks.

[07:31] Dev Patel: Yeah.

[07:33] Talia Benson: I’ll add that to the escalation map. Like “if premium SLA, route to #marketplace-escalations.”

[07:42] Rafael Mendes: From SRE side, premium doesn’t change the incident response. Outage is outage.

[07:47] Jasmine Liu: Makes sense.

[07:49] Elliot Price: For customer comms, we’ll have docs plus status page references. But marketplace buyers tend to go to AWS support first sometimes.

[07:58] Dev Patel: Oh yeah, good point. We should put in the doc: “Contact Redwood Support for activation issues,” not AWS.

[08:05] Jasmine Liu: Do we need a macro if they say “AWS told me to contact you”?

[08:09] Dev Patel: Yes, a polite one.

[08:12] Elliot Price: Also GCP marketplace has that “deployment validation” step where they want you to click through a configuration. If they fail that, they think Redwood is broken.

[08:23] Leila Farouk: In staging the region mismatch error message was not super clear. It said “invalid location,” like generic.

[08:31] Chloe Martin: We updated it in the latest build. It now says, “Your marketplace purchase is for region X; your Redwood org is set to Y. Switch org region or contact support.” Something like that.

[08:43] Jasmine Liu: Can you send Support a screenshot of those states? Because support replies are so much easier with the exact UI.

[08:49] Chloe Martin: Yeah. I’ll do that. Some of the text might change but close enough.

[08:55] Dev Patel: Also, region change is not self-serve in all cases, right? Mina owns routing policies; region is tricky.

[09:03] Jasmine Liu: Mina’s not on the call, but we can capture a rule: if region mismatch, Support confirms where they need to run and then escalates for region migration if needed.

[09:13] Rafael Mendes: Please, just, region migrations can have data residency implications. We shouldn’t promise same-day.

[09:19] Jasmine Liu: Good call. We’ll use careful wording.

[09:23] Markus Klein: Field perspective: buyers care about “EU region” language a lot. If they purchased in EU and it ends up in US, it’s a deal-killer.

[09:32] Jasmine Liu: Yep.

[09:34] Jasmine Liu: Okay, billing/invoice confusion. Dev, what’s Support’s line?

[09:38] Dev Patel: For marketplace charges, the invoice comes from AWS or GCP. Redwood can’t alter it. We can explain usage meters in Redwood, but not the marketplace invoice.

[09:49] Dev Patel: If they’re seeing both marketplace and direct contract charges, that’s a bigger issue. Usually it’s because they have two orgs or they didn’t turn off the old plan.

[10:00] Ethan Park: Or they have a direct API key in one org and marketplace entitlement in another. That happens.

[10:06] Dev Patel: Yep. So macro should ask: “Which Redwood org ID? Which API key? Are you using a key created before marketplace purchase?”

[10:14] Jasmine Liu: And escalation for billing goes to Finance, right? Laura Bennett’s team.

[10:20] Dev Patel: Correct. But Support should triage first to confirm if it’s actually a billing problem or just usage reporting confusion.

[10:29] Elliot Price: We can also add a docs paragraph on “marketplace billing vs Redwood usage analytics.” People expect them to match line-by-line and they won’t.

[10:38] Jasmine Liu: Great.

[10:40] Jasmine Liu: Security packet requests: what’s the workflow? We don’t want Support sending the wrong thing.

[10:46] Markus Klein: Please do not send SOC2 report without NDA. Olga will kill us.

[10:52] Jasmine Liu: (laughs) Yes.

[10:54] Elliot Price: On docs, we can publish the “security overview” and high-level statements. For SOC2 report, we route request to GRC.

[11:03] Dev Patel: So macro: “We can share a security overview immediately; for SOC 2 report and pen test letter we’ll coordinate under NDA.” Then we open an internal request to Olga Petrov / Aisha Rahman.

[11:15] Jasmine Liu: Perfect.

[11:17] Talia Benson: Can we also define what information Support needs before escalating to Eng? Like we don’t want a vague “entitlement broken” ping.

[11:25] Rafael Mendes: Yes. Please include provider, timestamp, customer identifier, and if possible the request ID from Console. We have tracing.

[11:33] Allison Grant: And include whether it’s AWS or GCP plus which SKU. Because sometimes the mapping is wrong, not the webhook.

[11:42] Jasmine Liu: Okay, let’s capture an “intake checklist.” Dev can you read it back as you’d want in a macro.

[11:48] Dev Patel: Sure. For entitlement/provisioning:

[11:52] Dev Patel: 1) Marketplace provider: AWS or GCP.
2) Approx purchase time and timezone.
3) Screenshot of marketplace subscription page (redact as needed).
4) Redwood org ID and org name.
5) Email of the Redwood org admin who is contacting us.
6) Region they purchased in and region they are trying to use.
7) Any error message text from Console.

[12:14] Dev Patel: Optional but great: request ID / correlation ID from Console.

[12:20] Chloe Martin: The Console shows a “Support ID” now in some error states. I’ll confirm if it’s in the build going out.

[12:28] Leila Farouk: In E2E tests it showed up on the region mismatch flow but not on the entitlement pending flow.

[12:34] Chloe Martin: Right, that’s what I remember too.

[12:37] Jasmine Liu: Okay.

[12:39] Markus Klein: Another one: customers will ask “can we switch from marketplace to direct contract later” or upgrades/downgrades. Support should have a line.

[12:49] Dev Patel: Yeah. We can say: “Yes, we can support a transition; talk to your account team.” But we should not promise instant upgrades because the entitlement change might take time.

[13:01] Ethan Park: Entitlement updates are event-based. It should be relatively quick, but… there are edge cases.

[13:07] Rafael Mendes: And if AWS is delayed, we can’t force it.

[13:11] Jasmine Liu: So conservative language.

[13:13] Jasmine Liu: Let’s move to playbooks. Dev, what runbooks exist now?

[13:18] Dev Patel: We have a draft “Marketplace provisioning troubleshooting guide” in Confluence, but it’s a little old. It includes steps like: check entitlement state in admin panel, verify webhook received, verify org linking.

[13:30] Dev Patel: I want to add “if entitlement lag > 20 minutes, page SRE.” And link the dashboards Rafael mentioned.

[13:38] Rafael Mendes: I’ll give you the exact Grafana links.

[13:41] Allison Grant: And the alert runbook. It’s in the observability pack, but I’ll paste the internal link.

[13:47] Elliot Price: For customer-facing doc, we’ll keep it lighter. Like “here’s how to link your org, here’s what to do if it says pending, here’s support contact.” We won’t include internal dashboards obviously.

[14:01] Jasmine Liu: Great.

[14:03] Jasmine Liu: Leila, can you share what we learned from the staging activation delay incident?

[14:08] Leila Farouk: Yeah, it was a retry/idempotency thing. The web hook came twice, first time partially processed, second time got dropped because it thought it was a duplicate, but it wasn’t fully applied. So entitlement stayed in “pending.”

[14:25] Ethan Park: That’s the bug we fixed with the hotfix PR. We also added a backfill script.

[14:31] Dev Patel: So in the runbook we should include: “If stuck, run backfill job,” but Support can’t run it, so it’s an escalation.

[14:39] Ethan Park: Correct. Support should capture identifiers and escalate to Eng on-call.

[14:45] Jasmine Liu: Okay.

[14:47] Jasmine Liu: Anything else likely to break on launch day?

[14:51] Rafael Mendes: Signature validation differences between AWS and GCP. If the config is wrong, we’ll see webhook validation failures.

[14:59] Ethan Park: Also, customers using multiple AWS accounts. They purchase in one account, then try to link from another. We need Console copy plus support guidance.

[15:09] Chloe Martin: We added copy: “Make sure you are logged into the same AWS account that completed the purchase.” But, you know, people ignore it.

[15:17] Dev Patel: So that’s a macro too.

[15:20] Jasmine Liu: Okay. Let’s do a quick run through each category and define escalation owner.

[15:26] Jasmine Liu: 1) Entitlement delay. Support triage, then if >15 minutes and no incident, escalate to Eng (Ethan’s rotation?) or SRE if alerting triggered.

[15:37] Ethan Park: Yes. For suspected pipeline issue, SRE. For suspected mapping issue, Eng.

[15:43] Rafael Mendes: Works.

[15:45] Jasmine Liu: 2) Wrong org linking. Support triage + identity verification, then Console backend (Chloe).

[15:52] Chloe Martin: Yes, but if it’s a security concern, loop Marcus Lin. But for routine admin mistakes, Console team.

[16:00] Jasmine Liu: 3) Region mismatch. Support triage and then… who approves region changes?

[16:06] Ethan Park: Platform. Mina usually. But I can route initially.

[16:10] Jasmine Liu: Okay: Support -> Platform via Ethan.

[16:14] Jasmine Liu: 4) Billing/invoice. Support triage then Finance/Legal.

[16:20] Dev Patel: Yes.

[16:21] Jasmine Liu: 5) Security docs. Support sends public security overview, routes SOC2/pen test requests to Olga/Aisha.

[16:29] Elliot Price: And we should encourage them to use the marketplace listing attachments if present.

[16:34] Markus Klein: Right, but we have to keep attachments consistent with reality. No over-claiming.

[16:40] Jasmine Liu: Yep.

[16:41] Jasmine Liu: Alright, templates. Dev, do you already have draft macro text?

[16:46] Dev Patel: Not yet. I’ll write it after this and share for review.

[16:50] Jasmine Liu: Please include a “friendly but firm” line about timelines and what we can’t do. Like we can’t change AWS invoices.

[16:58] Dev Patel: Yep.

[17:00] Jasmine Liu: Elliot, where will the customer-facing FAQ live?

[17:04] Elliot Price: In docs site under “Getting started -> Procurement / Marketplace.” We’ll have separate pages:

[17:10] Elliot Price: - AWS Marketplace: prerequisites, purchase steps, link your Redwood org, verify entitlement.
- GCP Marketplace: similar but with a section on validation steps and regions.

[17:22] Elliot Price: Plus FAQ: refunds, upgrades/downgrades, support contact, billing expectations.

[17:29] Jasmine Liu: Okay. And Support replies should link to those.

[17:33] Dev Patel: Right. We’ll use the doc links in macros.

[17:37] Talia Benson: Timing wise, docs need to be live same day as listings. Because partner reviewers click links.

[17:44] Elliot Price: Understood.

[17:46] Jasmine Liu: Rafael, what Slack channel should Support use for urgent escalations?

[17:51] Rafael Mendes: #marketplace-onboarding for general, and #sre-oncall for paging, but please don’t spam. Better is to page via PagerDuty if Sev-1 criteria.

[18:02] Dev Patel: Can we write down Sev-1 criteria in the runbook?

[18:05] Rafael Mendes: Yes. Something like: multiple customers cannot activate entitlements, webhook failures spike, or provisioning pipeline down.

[18:13] Allison Grant: We can also base it on alert firing. If “webhook_validation_failures” alert is firing, treat as Sev-1.

[18:21] Jasmine Liu: Great.

[18:23] Jasmine Liu: Quick note—some tickets will come in through Sales/SE too. Markus, can your team route them correctly?

[18:30] Markus Klein: Yes, but we need the same intake checklist. SEs sometimes just Slack “it’s broken.”

[18:36] Jasmine Liu: (laughs) We’ll give you a copy-paste checklist.

[18:40] Markus Klein: Perfect.

[18:42] Jasmine Liu: Any last concerns?

[18:45] Chloe Martin: Just that our error messages might still say “market place” in one spot. I saw it in a build.

[18:51] Dev Patel: That’s fine. Support can translate.

[18:54] Ethan Park: One more: if a customer has multiple AWS payer accounts (like consolidated billing), they might not know which account “owns” the marketplace subscription.

[19:06] Dev Patel: So we ask for a screenshot of the subscription page, and if they can’t find it, we ask them to confirm the payer vs linked accounts.

[19:14] Jasmine Liu: Good.

[19:16] Jasmine Liu: Okay, recap and next steps.

[19:19] Jasmine Liu: Dev will draft macros + tags and share for review by Friday.

[19:23] Jasmine Liu: Rafael will send dashboard links and confirm alert thresholds plus on-call routing.

[19:28] Jasmine Liu: Elliot will confirm final doc URLs for AWS and GCP marketplace onboarding and FAQ.

[19:33] Jasmine Liu: Chloe will send screenshots of Console states and confirm the “Support ID” behavior.

[19:38] Jasmine Liu: Ethan will send us the exact identifiers to request from customers for AWS and GCP entitlement investigations.

[19:45] Jasmine Liu: Leila will run staging E2E flows and note expected timings.

[19:50] Jasmine Liu: Talia will send an escalation map for launch week.

[19:55] Jasmine Liu: Anything I missed?

[19:57] (crosstalk)

[20:00] Rafael Mendes: Sounds good.

[20:01] Dev Patel: All set.

[20:03] Jasmine Liu: Alright, thanks everyone.

[End]

Note: Transcript is auto-generated; speaker attribution and terminology may be imperfect.
